test_title: PYST 72: RRB Group D - GA (Held On: 29 Dec, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Which international agency raised concerns leading to amendments in India’s anti-doping law in July 2025?

options.text: United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO)

solution:
The correct answer is __**World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA)** is the primary international body responsible for regulating and monitoring the fight against drugs in sports. In **July 2025**, India introduced critical amendments to its **National Anti-Doping Act** following concerns raised by **WADA** regarding compliance with the **World Anti-Doping Code**.
 
• The amendments aimed to ensure that India's legal framework for sports remains consistent with **international standards**, specifically addressing the independence of the **National Anti-Doping Agency (NADA)** and the **National Anti-Doping Laboratory (NDTL)**.
 
• The **World Anti-Doping Code** is a document that harmonizes anti-doping policies, rules, and regulations within sport organizations and among public authorities around the world. Failure to comply with this code can lead to sanctions, including the suspension of a country's ability to host international sporting events. ***Hence, the statement regarding WADA raising concerns is correct.***
 
• In the context of the **2025** legislative update, the focus was on enhancing **data protection** for athletes and streamlining the **results management** process to prevent delays in adjudicating doping cases.
 
• The **National Anti-Doping Agency (NADA)** of India, established in **2005**, is mandated to implement anti-doping programs in the country in accordance with **WADA** guidelines.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA):**
 
 
• **WADA** was established on **November 10, 1999**, in **Lausanne, Switzerland**, following the **Declaration of Lausanne**. Its current headquarters are located in **Montreal, Canada**.
 
• It is a **foundation** initiated by the **International Olympic Committee (IOC)** to promote, coordinate, and monitor the fight against doping in sports in all its forms.
 
 
 
• **UNESCO’s Role:**
 
 
• The **United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO)** adopted the **International Convention against Doping in Sport** in **2005**.
 
• This convention is the legal instrument through which governments formally commit to the **WADA Code**, as **WADA** is a private non-governmental organization.
 
 
 
• **International Olympic Committee (IOC):**
 
 
• While the **IOC** works closely with **WADA**, its primary function is the organization and governance of the **Olympic Games** and the promotion of **Olympism** worldwide.
 
• The **IOC** provides significant funding to **WADA**, but the agency operates as an independent international body.
 
 
 
• **National Anti-Doping Bill, 2022:**
 
 
• Before the **2025** amendments, India passed the **National Anti-Doping Bill in 2022**, which provided statutory backing to **NADA** and established the **National Board for Anti-Doping in Sports**.
 
• This legislative framework is essential for maintaining the **National Anti-Doping Laboratory (NDTL)**’s **WADA accreditation**, which is necessary for the international validity of test results.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Banned Substances:** **WADA** maintains an annual **Prohibited List**, which identifies substances and methods prohibited at all times, in-competition only, and in specific sports (e.g., **anabolic agents**, **peptide hormones**, and **masking agents**).
 
• **Whereabouts Requirements:** Athletes in a **Registered Testing Pool (RTP)** must provide accurate information about their daily location to facilitate **out-of-competition testing** without prior notice.
 
• **Therapeutic Use Exemptions (TUE):** Athletes may have illnesses or conditions that require them to take particular medications. If the medication falls under the **Prohibited List**, a **TUE** may give the athlete the authorization to take the needed medicine.
 
• **Sanctions:** Violations of anti-doping rules can lead to **disqualification** of results, **forfeiture** of medals, and **period of ineligibility** (bans) ranging from a few months to a lifetime.
